[check 6] At 360px the page is 389px wide, 29px of horizontal scroll. Find the element wider than the column (a fixed width, a nowrap line, desktop-size type) and fit it to 360px.
[check 6] At 360px, text runs past the edge of the screen and is cut: "Designed." (x 40 to 389), "The fidelity creed, lifted from my own c" (x 40 to 382). Set display type in clamp() with a vw term so it fits the column, and let lines wrap.

1. (Judgment 6) At 1440 the left spine shows only the mark, "Doug March" and the role line. The declared vertical index (Work / About / Contact, `nav_form: list`, small-caps, one amber hairline per row, 44px rows) is missing from the rail entirely. Add it beneath the role line so desktop visitors have navigation.

2. (Judgment 5) The site callout says "only the human merges the one that ships." The dougmar.ch record says the opposite: "It redesigns itself unattended. Nothing may wait on me approving it before it ships." Rewrite the line so it agrees with the record.

3. (Judgment 2) In the 1440 rail, the wordmark "Doug March" is wider than the 96px spine. The "D" is clipped at the left edge and the "h" runs into the amber rule on the right, so the name does not read cleanly. Set it to fit the rail, for example by stacking "Doug / March" or reducing the step.

4. (Judgment 2) On the amber signal band, "▼ −1.96%" is set in dark amber on the amber field and nearly disappears. Set it in the declared `fieldInkMuted` ink, as the brief specifies, so it reads against the band.

5. (Judgment 3) The composition declares two equal columns, mirrored across the gutter, with the lead-in and the day's facts placed by distance from the marquee. At 1440 the whole hero sits in the left column and the right half of the field is empty, so nothing is mirrored and there is no radial pull toward "Designed." Bring the mirrored counterpart into the right column, or centre the lockup on the gutter axis, so the declared structure is visible.

6. (Judgment 6) At 360 the nav band breaks "Contact" onto a second line under "Work / About". The declaration calls for a single small-caps row with amber rules. Fit all three links on one row.

The page commits to its one idea: a heavy italic Fraunces "Designed." in chalk amber, low on an ultramarine field, resolves the lighter lead-in above it, and the empty blueprint field and the amber spine rules let that word carry the argument at 1440 and at 360.
